A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HiCache and retain matching methods, experiments, and theoretical material. All 17 pages of v1 and 27 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and super-resolution benchmarks, contraction-factor ablations, Gaussianity tests, and feature-prediction simulations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline comparisons, adaptive-scaling experiments, broader Gaussianity tests, and Qwen-Image and Chipmunk experiments.

M1.justification: The cached finite-difference predictor and scaled-Hermite basis remain unchanged. v2 adds an optional HiCache-Adaptive procedure that computes capped per-layer scaling from an EMA-style estimate of feature-difference magnitudes (appendix Equations 41–42), plus a scaling-only TaylorSeer variant. These extend the existing method without replacing its core procedure.

E1.justification: The four task domains and named benchmarks—DrawBench, VBench, ImageNet, and DIV8K—remain. Qwen-Image, FLUX.1-schnell, and accelerator combinations add model configurations within retained tasks; no distinct new dataset or input domain is established. The changed DrawBench prompt count concerns E3.

E2.justification: The FLUX comparison expands from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 3 with ClusCa, TeaCache, Chipmunk, and DBCache. The DiT comparison adds Delta-DiT, L2C, and SmoothCache in v2 Table 4. Qualitative comparator membership also changes, including adding DuCa to the detail-preservation comparison. Taylor and TaylorSeer are matched as the same method.

E3.justification: The stated DrawBench sample size changes from 1,632 to 200, without establishing that retained experiments were rerun. Added protocols include Qwen-Image at 1328×1328 with 50 steps, short-step FLUX.1-schnell configurations, and controlled adaptive-scaling and Chipmunk comparisons. Additional Gaussianity evaluations cover six layers, 15 layer–module configurations, and separate denoising phases.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's contraction sweep and trajectory simulations, v2 adds a scaling-only Hi-Taylor control (Table 2), adaptive-versus-fixed scaling tests (Table 7), and layer- and phase-specific Gaussianity analysis (Table 6). ClusCa and Chipmunk combinations also test compatibility with other accelerators. These substantially expand evidence about mechanism, stability, and applicability.

E5.justification: v2 first specifies 500 parametric bootstrap simulations and a p-value threshold of 0.05 for its additional Gaussianity tests; v1 only reports p-values of 1.0 for 25 configurations. Neither PDF provides concrete repeated-run counts, seed details, or uncertainty intervals for benchmark performance. v2's affirmative checklist answers do not supply those missing details.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including ClusCa versus Hi-ClusCa ImageReward of 0.9480 versus 0.9840, Qwen-Image interval-8 scores of 0.750 versus 0.844 for TaylorSeer versus HiCache, and 73/75 passing mid-phase Gaussianity tests. Most original HiCache benchmark scores remain unchanged. Some reduced-step and CLIP entries disappear, while TaylorSeer's FLUX N=7 latency changes from 4.93 to 4.84 seconds.

T1.justification: v2 adds local-linearization and Berry–Esseen propositions with proofs, Gaussian-weighted projection optimality, and a Hermite envelope lemma. It replaces the erroneous unconditional factorial-convergence comparison with a contraction-dependent claim for moderate orders. Section 3 also distinguishes projection-optimal fitted coefficients from the implemented finite-difference approximation. Some older, broader theoretical statements remain.

C1.justification: The central Hermite-plus-scaling acceleration contribution remains. v2 adds explicit claims that scaling helps TaylorSeer independently and that HiCache upgrades other forecasting pipelines, illustrated with ClusCa. The abstract corrects the above-baseline FLUX speedup claim from 6.24× to 5.55×, consistent with the reported ImageReward values.

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantive qualifications about conditional convergence and approximate rather than automatically optimal prediction, although broader assertions persist elsewhere. New appendix discussion identifies mid-transition Gaussianity exceptions, explains adaptive scaling's protection against aggressive settings, and interprets Chipmunk integration as complementary acceleration. Super-resolution discussion now explicitly quantifies the retained quality loss instead of relying only on near-lossless language.

D1.justification: v1's extensive Python implementation in Appendix A.7 is removed, while the promise of future code release becomes a repository link in v2. v2 newly discloses DiT's sigma=0.75, adaptive-scaling initialization and caps, and execution details for added configurations. This materially changes reproducibility information; repository availability and contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including ClusCa, Chipmunk, DBCache, Delta-DiT, L2C, SmoothCache, and Qwen-Image, while removing several earlier references. It more explicitly positions HiCache as an upgrade compatible with existing forecasting and sparse accelerators. The overall related-work taxonomy remains, and TaylorSeer/ToCa bibliographic updates represent the same prior methods.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites the contribution list, method exposition, results narrative, discussion, and conclusion. Separate task-result subsections are consolidated into Section 4.2, supplementary material is reorganized, and ethics, reproducibility-checklist, and AI-assistance sections are added. The title also changes to emphasize the plug-in role.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to predominantly single-column layout, with extensively rebuilt tables and qualitative grids. v1 Figures 3–4 merge into v2 Figure 3, Figures 6–7 merge into Figure 5, and the trajectory-order figure moves to the appendix. The super-resolution plot is redrawn, and Tables 6–9 add new displays.

improvement.justification: v2 improves empirical support through the scaling-only control, accelerator integration tests, and broader Gaussianity diagnostics, and corrects the unsupported 6.24× above-baseline claim. The overall gain is limited: theoretical qualifications coexist with retained overclaims, notably appendix Remark 1 versus Corollary 2; benchmark uncertainty remains undocumented; and removing the Python listing reduces self-contained reproducibility. The repository link does not establish from the PDFs that this loss is repaired.
